newsitem.title: CANADA: Winnipeg to launch global air freight operation.
newsitem.headline: Winnipeg to launch global air freight operation.

text.p: A local consortium said its plan to launch a global air service for freight forwarders has advanced to the stage of securing aircraft and financing for a launch next May or June.

Winnport, whose partners include Winnipeg International Airport, Air Canada, two national railways, a major bank as well as freight and trucking companies, will start with a pair of Boeing 747-200 freighters, executive vice-president Gordon Johnstone said.
The service, called Forwarder Direct, will use Winnipeg as its main hub and target the nearby U.S. market, particularly the midwest and western states.
Initially, Forwarder Direct will offer five flights weekly to eastern Asia, plus two to Europe and one to India, document issued by Winnport show.

Johnstone said Forwarder Direct also may serve Montreal's Mirabel International Airport, which is 6-8 hours by road from Toronto, New York and Boston and already a freighter stop for Air France and Lufthansa Cargo.
Both Winnipeg and Mirabel are 24-hour airports. Air Canada has a maintenance base at Winnipeg airport.

Both airports expect to be designated special duty-free foreign trade zones by the time Forwarder Direct is launched. Both are in remote locations - with ample space available for construction of warehousing and distribution facilities.
Johnstone said more details will be made public by the end of September.
Studies have confirmed the viability of the Winnipeg hub scheme, said Johnstone.
"We're finalizing that now but we're pretty sure that we've got something."
Road feeder links will radiate from Winnipeg - which is about the geographic midpoint of North America, 90 kilometres from the Canada-U.S. border - to cities across the United States.
From the U.S. border, Winnipeg is less than a day's drive from Minneapolis, Milwaukee, Chicago, Salt Lake City, Kansas City and Denver using the U.S.interstate highway system.

The consortium says it will build permanent handling facilities at the airport, and provide customers with a complete Electronic Data InterChange(EDI) capability for real-time tracking of shipments. EDI network provider Transport Data Network International is one of the consortium's partners.
The key selling point of the Winnport plan is that it minimizes the length of the air haul to Asia by offering the most direct polar routing for customers in the U.S. Midwest.
Winnport officials believe Forwarder Direct will attract less time-sensitive air freight in search of lower rates.
Johnstone said the consortium is looking at a number of options to acquire freighters, but would not elaborate.
Winnport had eyed two Air Canada B-747-200 combis for freighter conversion, but the airline now plans to keep operating them as combis.
Winnport said it is exploring how to secure up to C$120 million in startup equity among its current investors, potential customers and key institutional investors.

It added it has applied to the Canadian government for the necessary licencing and bilateral route authorities to act as a scheduled all-cargo airline. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
